wld_farmer.text: Now then. Chalk, this, all the way down. Grows grand barley and lousy ponds. My granddad's sheep never knew a stream.
See the roofs? Pantiles. Orange clay, curled like an S, made just over the Humber and shipped in from the Low Countries before that. Every barn in East Yorkshire wears a pantile hat.

wld_flint.text: The ploughs bring up flints every winter. Black inside, white crust, sharp as a tongue. Folk here built walls with them and Stone Age folk made arrowheads.
Plenty for everyone. Take a handful, the field won't miss them.

else.text: That's today's lot. Come back tomorrow, the plough'll have turned up more.

wld_hare.text: Brown hares, out on the open wolds. In spring the females box the males off when they get too keen. Everybody thinks it's two lads fighting. It's a lass saying no.
Hares never dig burrows. They lie up in a scrape in the grass called a form, and trust their legs.
